parsed.rationale: In sinus rhythm there are QS complexes in V1–V4 and deep, symmetric T-wave inversion in V2–V5, which fits an anterior MI that has already evolved; the ST elevation in V2–V3 is only about 1–1.5 mm, so it does not meet the usual STEMI cut-off of ≥2 mm on this tracing alone (it would meet the ≥1.5 mm cut-off for women), although the final diagnosis you mention can still be correct from serial ECGs and troponins.
